utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning all. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For the Stanisic Defence, Slobodan Zecevic. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic, Dragan Krgovic, Mr. Eric Tully, and our lovely assistant Ms. Harriet Taylor. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the witness return to the courtroom, please. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I was just preparing for cross-examination. Nothing else. Well, I know Your Honours are so conscious about time, so that's why --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Yesterday when we finished our session, I addressed the Chamber. I owe certain explanations to honourable Judge Harhoff regarding some questions that I put to Colonel Basara yesterday. In particular, when I asked him a part of line of my questions regarding the episodes where he personally came to Manjaca to bring out young Muslim, Nijaz, and also on the other occasion when he personally and -- ordered two of his soldiers to go to school in Sanski Most to get out two Muslims to make a favour to the father of these young people when he know -- knew him before, the line was very simple. We tried to show that Colonel Basara, being a military commander, in his zone of responsibility was able to sort of act whenever he found its necessary to bring people in detention or to get them out. And our theory, Your Honour, is that in accordance with the international criminal law, case law, within this Tribunal and the international humanity law as well as the local domestic jurisdiction, that military commander during the armed conflict is the supreme master or person for particular zone of responsibility. And that of course all other forces, including police forces, should be and will be subordinate to him in certain aspect of civilian life of course. More details we shall hear from OTP witness Mrs. Hanson, Dorothea Hanson, and other witnesses as well as from OTP side and Defence side. That was the line of question which I followed yesterday with Colonel Basara, who testified. If it pleases the Court, this explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't want to waste any more time, and I'm not going to, but I don't think it's appropriate for counsel to make speeches like this. I appreciate Mr. Pantelic says he was answering the question, but that's a speech and the time for speeches is not during the evidence. Speeches are for the end of the trial or at the stage where there's a submission of no case to answer. But I don't think that speeches like this are appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, I respectfully disagree that that was a speech. It was just a part of Defence strategy to be shown -- explained to the Trial Chamber. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Counsels, let's not waste any more time. My understanding of Mr. Pantelic's intervention was a response to a question that I actually did put to him yesterday, but of course I agree that this is too early for the concluding remarks. Should we get the witness in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Djekanovic, good morning to you. As would have -- as I believe we would have explained to you on -- when we took the -- when you were stood down on Friday, it isn't always possible to predict how long witnesses will take and, therefore, you're returning on Wednesday, a little later than you or the Chamber would have anticipated. But the -- I would remind you that where we are is that counsel for the Prosecution has completed her examination-in-chief and now it remains for you to be cross-examined. I would remind you that you're still on your oath, and in that vein I would remind you that the obligation of your oath to give truthful testimony carries with it the sanction of penalties for testimony that is false. Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Djekanovic.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I hope you've managed to have a good rest over the past three days. Mr. Djekanovic, during your first day of examination, on page 8 of the transcript and on page 51 of the transcript, you discussed with the Prosecutor the issue of the community of municipalities of Banja Luka and its relationship with the autonomous region of Krajina. When I read the transcript, I found out that it was not quite clearly recorded, and I would appreciate some clarification for the benefit of all of us, including the Trial Chamber. Now, the union of municipalities or the community of municipalities was a regional structure that existed in the former Yugoslavia as well, not only in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Those unions of municipalities, those regional unions of municipalities, were constituted for geographic, economic, and other considerations whereby it was in the interests of municipalities to form an association and that's why they did it; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, this union of municipalities had a certain structure that reflected the structure of single municipalities. It had Assemblies and other agencies?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not involved in politics, and I cannot answer you clearly whether these structures were identical, but it's quite certain in any case that all those unions of municipalities had all the various bodies which had their jurisdiction each.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand. I'm sorry that you are a mechanical engineer by training. Just one question: Was the union -- did the union of municipalities of Banja Luka have an Assembly, a parliament?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So in 1991, when the Assembly of the union of municipalities of Banja Luka became the Assembly of the autonomous region of Krajina, it was just a case of re-naming, wasn't it? I'll ask you about that later. I know you are about to tell me that some other municipalities joined at that point. But formally speaking, it was just a change of name and the joining of the union by some additional municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So in that context, the continuity of the municipality of Kotor Varos and the union of municipalities of Banja Luka, later the autonomous region of Krajina has lasted from the 1980s, 1980-something when the union of municipalities of Banja Luka was created?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that's why you said in your answer that you in the SDS did not raise this issue as a priority, because it was a very well-known fact already by that time?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in addition to this autonomous region of Krajina, there was also a Croatian union of municipalities called Herceg-Bosna; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Croatian community of municipalities, Herceg-Bosna, was created back in -- on 18 November 1991?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact date, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a map, a pre-war map of Bosnia and Herzegovina listing and showing all municipalities with their boundaries, and then I'd like to ask you to circle, to the best of your recollection, the municipalities which constituted Herceg-Bosna to the best of your ability.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show to the witness 1D00-4619.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you, Mr. Djekanovic, the interpreters have warned me that we are talking too fast. Will you please mind the pause between questions and answers, and I will take care too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we enlarge this map a little? Thank you. That's all right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see well on the map?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right then. The municipality of Livno, was it part of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please give the witness a pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please circle the municipality.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the future, please put a circle around the name of the municipality. Now Kupres, was it part of Herceg-Bosna; if so, put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Travnik?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Put a circle around it, it's in the middle, the very centre.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You just encircled Novi Travnik. Was it part of Herceg-Bosna as well?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Vitez, municipality of Vitez, was it part of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You put a circle around it. Thank you. Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Fojnica -- did you put a around Busovaca, it's below Vitez, a bit to the right.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's it. Fojnica, was it part of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's to the right of Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Kresevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Konjic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Prozor?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tomislavgrad -- sorry, at the time it was called Duvno?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Posusje?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did we mention Jablanica? Yes, you put a circle around it. Mostar?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostar was the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Siroki Brijeg, then called Listica?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we raise the map, please, just 2 centimetres -- oh, sorry, now you can't do it, now you can't do it because it's marked. We didn't position it too well, but never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In addition there was Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Citluk?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Capljina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Trebinje wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Part of Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, part of Trebinje was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then Jajce, put a circle around Jajce.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember about Kakanj, I can't tell you, but Zepce was part of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then put a circle around it. Fine. Now, the municipalities we have enumerated in addition to those we can't see on this map because we didn't position it well formed the Croatian community of municipalities Herceg-Bosna from 18 November 1991, although you don't recall the date?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I think Kotor Varos joined also.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's take it one step at a time. We'll come to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please get a number for this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D20, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get again 1D4619 [as interpreted] again, but this time raise it a bit higher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have to emphasise that Derventa, Brod, Samac municipalities were also part of this community.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We are coming to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the whole map of Bosnia and Herzegovina so the witness can show us. Just a bit smaller, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Now, can you see well on this map? You know what? Just put a little cross or a dot on the municipalities that were part of Herceg-Bosna. Right. Go ahead now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness get some help -- no wait a bit. Can the witness start marking now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Wait a second -- no, no, no, please don't do anything until the map is positioned. This is the AV service which usually works very well with occasional hitches. Now start.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And mark all those you marked on the previous map, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Kresevo, Fojnica, Konjic. Konjic and Kresevo I believe you didn't mark. You didn't mark Konjic and Kresevo. You marked Mostar, Capljina, did you? So this is roughly what the Croatian community of the municipalities of Herceg-Bosna looked like in 1991, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we assign an exhibit number to this document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 1D21, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Djekanovic, judging by the area of this Croatian community of municipalities, Herceg-Bosna, accounted for about a third of the overall area of Bosnia-Herzegovina, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about Ante Mandic as your community prefect. The SDS of the Kotor Varos municipality, irrespective of the party agreement in Sarajevo about the distribution of positions at municipal level did cede that position to the HDZ and Ante Mandic was appointed to that position, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That community prefect who was actually supported by you wanted to join Kotor Varos to this community, the Croatian communities of municipalities, and practically take it out of the Banja Luka union of municipalities to which it had belonged for so many years. Wasn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In contravention of the positions of the Municipal Assembly, he did decide to that effect. He signed an agreement to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you show on this map where your municipality of Kotor Varos is located and mark it with a large X.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this municipality of yours, Kotor Varos, was to be -- was to join the Croatian community of municipalities, that was the intention of Anto Mandic, although by its geographic position and by all other criteria it belonged to the Banja Luka region, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In that sense, Mr. Anto Mandic participated in the work of the community of Herceg-Bosna and effectively signed the -- signed a document about the municipality of Kotor Varos joining the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, although that was not the position of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When was that roughly?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in late 1991. I do not remember the exact date, as I said earlier, but it was toward the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this marked map into evidence also, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D22, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us pass on to something else, to another problem. If I remember well, in your examination-in-chief you were member of the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As a delegate?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a delegate I was elected delegate at the first multi-party elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You're speaking about 1990?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us shed some light on this issue for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. The Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia as a federation in 1991 was in existence, and it was in 1992 until sometime in April, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but before that Slovenia had adopted a decision about unilateral separation, and I believe Croatia too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the issue of the secession of two republics does not mean --

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, at that moment. Yes, at that moment the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was still in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you remember that as early as February 1991 Alija Izetbegovic tried to initiate a vote about the declaration on the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the Assembly? Were you present at that Assembly meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present at all Assembly meetings, at all sessions; and since the beginning, that is, since that Assembly started functioning, it was clear that things would develop in that direction. There were such -- such tendencies at the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Our time is limited, so I would ask you to limit yourself to answering the question. This is not a crucial issue for what we are talking about, but it does provide a context. So do you agree with me that in February 1991 Alija Izetbegovic for the first time tried to push a declaration on the sovereignty of BiH through the Assembly but it didn't -- he wasn't successful at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was the structure of Bosnia-Herzegovina such that there were three constitutive people which, in essence, means that all three peoples constituted that republic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So there were mechanisms that prevented any one people to be down voted or two peoples joining forces against the third; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: However, in spite of all these constitutional and other legal limitations, in October 1991 the HDZ, that is, the members of parliament belonging to that party and to the SDA, passed a decision on the declaration of independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the night of the 14th through the 15th October or the 15th to the 16th?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That decision was passed in an illegal manner and contrary to your constitution; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Even the session of parliament which was interrupted or which had been interrupted was continued in a way contrary to the rules of procedure; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if I may call it that, your fellow members of parliament who belonged to the HDZ and the SDA parties in the Assembly in effect, by force and in -- illegally, contrary to the constitution, voted about the sovereignty and the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina in October 1991; isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the president of the SDS, Radovan Karadzic, asking them not to do that, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, there is much talk here about the position of the SDS being to preserve the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and that is then put into some virtual context of a Greater Serbia, et cetera. Tell me, apart from the SDS, the SKSDP, and the SRSJ, that is, parties who were -- that were also represented in parliament, the parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina, since the multi-party elections, were those parties also in favour of preserving the SFRJ and Bosnia as part of the SFRJ?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly the SDS at that time politically acted to preserve Yugoslavia. In that period there were also other Yugoslav-oriented political parties that also wanted to preserve Yugoslavia, among them the ones that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were there others?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- those were the early days of multi-party political life, and there weren't so many parties apart from the League of Communists that had survived. There was some reformists also that were in favour of preserving Yugoslavia. The reformists were a wing of the former League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, now I remember too. Thank you. Tell me, after that the Serbian people held a referendum that was attended -- or rather, the turn-out at the referendum of over 99 per cent and that referendum corroborated the wish of the Serbian people to remain in Yugoslavia, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Irrespective of this situation, that is, the declaration about sovereignty which was an illegal decision contrary to the constitution, which was passed by force, did you as a party and do you personally as a Member of Parliament continue going to the sessions of the BiH parliament?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that until the end of December we attended the common sessions. By that time we also tried to -- or rather, we tried to preserve all that, but as it became clear that we would be unsuccessful we left the Assembly very soon and established a separate Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the decision passed on the 18th of December addressed to the Presidency or the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina, asking for recognition -- just wait a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember all these decisions, but after all this time I cannot mention all these dates exactly. But I do remember the events, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At that moment when that illegal decision contrary to the constitution was passed about the -- about making the decision from October 1991 operational, you understood that it was no longer possible to go back; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief you said that the position of the SDS was to advocate centralisation rather than regionalisation or cantonisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the question. If you think -- if you mean the Republika Srpska, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well then obviously I didn't understand your answer either. So the SDS at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina advocated regionalisation, but in the context of the Republika Srpska that was created later he was -- it was in favour of centralisation, more or less?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know -- we're now speaking about Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you know that the regionalisation and cantonisation was absolutely supported by the European Union, wasn't it, in 1991 and in early 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, you are reminding me of that. You are keeping track of all this information. I do remember some plans, a Lisbon Plan and the attempt to create an atmosphere to avoid conflict, but those plans came to nothing; Alija Izetbegovic rejected them. Those negotiations and the solutions advocated by the European Union of the international factor implied a regionalisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina and certainly a different organisation -- organisational structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "Lisbon Plans," you mean the plan of the European Union popularly called Cutileiro's Plan?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the Cutileiro Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In essence, the Cutileiro Plan envisaged a regionalisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the effect of the creation of three communities that would have all structures of power and administration, and in Sarajevo there would be some sort of central power equal to that of a federal state?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that plan was crafted in Lisbon, but as soon as everybody got back to -- got back home it was rejected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just for the sake of better understanding, the Lisbon Plan or these Cutileiro Plans, would you please limit yourself to the question because your response may turn out differently in the transcript. So the Lisbon Agreement, under the auspices of the European Union chaired by Mr. Cutileiro, properly called the Cutileiro Plan, was signed by all three parties, major parties, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the SDA, HDZ, and SDA [as interpreted], that is, in other words, Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Izetbegovic, and Mr. Kljujic or whoever it was at the time, and they all accepted that plan in Lisbon, didn't they, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Upon returning to Sarajevo, Alija Izetbegovic withdrew his signature on that plan, did he?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djekanovic, let us speak a little about Crisis Staffs. You know that at the level of the Presidency of BiH, the Crisis Staff of the Presidency was established on the 21st of September, 1991, and the president of that staff was the member of the Presidency, Mr. Ejup Ganic, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were Crisis Staffs in all municipalities, also at the level of BiH and at the level of the Presidency, but I don't remember the dates when they were established, but there were Crisis Staffs all around.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the HDZ of Kotor Varos municipality established its own Crisis Staff which held meetings regularly, ever since February or March 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all three parties had Crisis Staffs at -- or in the territory of the Kotor Varos municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us show to the witness document 1D00-4000.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the document on your left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't. I've seen it here for the first time although I knew of its existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You see that the HDZ on the 8th of March, 1992, decided to establish a Crisis Staff and five individuals are mentioned here. Do you know anyone from Kotor Varos, any one of them?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pile Mandic, I knew him. I knew Ilija Zeba.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavo Petrusic I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you knew of its existence, and there's no reason for you to doubt the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't doubt it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As I understand his testimony, he wasn't the author, and he only became aware of it a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but he doesn't dispute the existence of the HDZ Crisis Staff at the time in Kotor Varos, and I asked him does he -- has any -- does he have any -- knowing all the situation in Kotor Varos, does he have any doubts as to the authenticity of this document. He says no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to -- I have no particular objection to this going in, although as I say the witness can't really deal with it. But I don't think that strict proof is really required by the Rules of this Tribunal. However, I am concerned it's not on the list that we were sent. Are there any other documents that aren't on our list? That's all I want to know?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it might be an oversight. I'm sorry. I apologise. Because this is the document which I used with the very first witness, and then I asked him do I need to -- can he confirm that the HDZ, the Crisis Staff existed and he says, "You don't have to show me the document," that is why I -- I'm sorry. But since this is our last witness from Kotor Varos, that is -- I thought that that would be the only appropriate point where I can offer this document because I wouldn't have any other opportunity, Your Honours. We don't intend to call any -- nor can we expect that any members of the HDZ Crisis Staff will testify in our case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It's admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D23, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know that apart from the Crisis Staff, the HDZ established an HVO command or headquarters for Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also said last time that at the time when the conflict broke out, especially in March, April, May, of a time before June, all three ethnic communities had commands of their own armed forces and that they had a large number of armed men organised into various units. And there was a display of this -- of these troops in the town there was even shooting. And once Mr. Anto Mandic was stopped at such a barricade that the members of the HVO and the Green Berets had put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, all three ethnic parties had some sort of military wing and there were commands of these persons who were established into units and the territory any one party tried to hold some check-points and barricades were put up where they stopped citizens. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot merely answer by yes or no because I would like to add an explanation. At that period the Serbian people was leaning on the Yugoslav People's Army, and at the time we didn't establish our own armed forces because there was this military force of the Yugoslav People's Army that we were relying on. But the Green Berets and the HVO were already established in the territory of the Kotor Varos municipality. Only later when the VRS was established or was being established, our formations were also established. So the SDS went about it in a different way, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The SDS didn't have a Crisis Staff in Kotor Varos municipality, as a party Crisis Staff, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian municipal office or municipality formed a Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djekanovic, can you please listen to my question. I'm asking you whether the SDS party formed its Crisis Staff just as you saw earlier that the HDZ formed its own Crisis Staff. Did the SDS in Kotor Varos have its Crisis Staff, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this was directly consequence of a decision by the SDS or the Serbian Assembly. I'm not quite sure about that, but there was a Crisis Staff, that is definite.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you formed -- when the Serbian Assembly formed the Crisis Staff, did you review the legal basis for that at the time, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about it last time --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, please, just answer with a yes or no if you can.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The legal basis for the establishment of the Crisis Staff was the Law on All People's Defence and social self protection, the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the strategy of All People's Defence; is that right? This would be the legal basis for the establishment of an organ such as the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I actually wanted to say in my answer to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To simplify things, the regulations provided that in extraordinary circumstances, even due to inclement weather or catastrophes caused by weather such collective organs be formed comprising the most responsible people in the municipality, who would take over the powers for the functioning of the municipality in such extraordinary circumstances because there was no possibility for the legally-elected municipal organs to convene. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When the Crisis Staff was formed, it became the sole authority in the municipality, uncontested power; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When I say "uncontested," what I mean by that is that all the rights and duties for normal life in the municipality, the economy, the utilities, the schools rested with the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all matters except for military matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In that sense you absolutely didn't require any instructions because the legal powers in that sense and the text of the law are very clear in terms of what are your powers, responsibilities, rights; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In order to form the Crisis Staff, you didn't have to resort or rely on any kind of instructions, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who made the preparations for the setting up of the Crisis Staff actually took as their basis the Law of All People's Defence. At the time when it was formed we were looking for a legal basis in those kinds of documents.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat exactly which documents he was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "documents," what do you mean? You mean legal -- laws?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the laws in force in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In that sense the duty of the Crisis Staff, as far as those laws were concerned, was that once the emergency situation had ended it was obliged to submit a report to the Municipal Assembly, which then the Municipal Assembly of a given municipality - in this case it was Kotor Varos - would adopt or not adopt the report and would decide on the responsibilities of the Crisis Staff members for their work?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In that sense it was not one of your duties to send reports to anyone about your work, except to keep records and minutes so that in your final report you would be able to report to the Municipal Assembly about your activities, what you did, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, we did not have any obligation to report to anyone about our work, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the examination-in-chief you said that from time to time you submitted a kind of summary report to the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of the Krajina in order to present the situation in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were just brief reports about some aspects of our work, but not a detailed report about all of our activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you said you didn't submit any reports, does that mean you didn't submit reports to any state organ: The government, the ministry, the Presidency, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't submit any such reports to those organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We've clarified this because that part was a little bit unclear during the examination-in-chief why you kept minutes of Crisis Staff meetings, so basically it was in order to document the proceedings on the basis of which you would compile reports that would be submitted to the Assembly of your socio-political community or the Municipal Assembly of Kotor Varos which could then agree to adopt it or reject it and establish your responsibility as members of the Crisis Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right, but here I would just like to add one sentence about those reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as the Dayton Accords were signed, I think that we were probably the first municipality to voluntarily hand over all those reports to the representatives of the international community. I think it was the IFOR at the time. Our secretariat took those documents to the Ramici base and made copies of all those documents. This was as soon as the Dayton reports were signed. So we voluntarily handed over those reports to them. We did not wish this to be a confidential procedure or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a question that should have been put to you by my learned friend, the Prosecutor, but I would like to help her. Can you please tell me, in September 1992 you had already set up a normal situation to a certain extent and the Executive Board of the municipality had started to function at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall when the municipality of Kotor Varos Assembly was re-convened again?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, I don't recall the exact date but parallel with the establishment of the Executive Board the Kotor Varos Municipal Assembly began to work, and it included the deputies who had been elected in 1990 if they were still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In any case, if you're unable to remember the date, this was in 1992, the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in 1992, end of 1992 in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to show to you a number of these minutes from Crisis Staff meetings, and we're not going to comment in detail on all of them, only some of them. But since you were the one who signed these reports we need to be able to tender them as exhibits in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown document 1D00-0749. [In English] Your Honours, just one indication. I believe I will finish right -- half an hour after the break, just an indication. That is the proximity as I can see at this moment. Thank you very much. I was notified by my learned colleague that this one was omitted to be sent to them again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's fine. So in that case --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll withdraw that one. Can I have 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I'm not objecting, I'm just pointing out without the microphone on --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, principles are principles, and we will follow the principles. I will withdraw this document. Thank you. Could the witness be shown 65 ter 00690. This one is definitely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Zecevic. We of course agree with your observation about principles, but if the Prosecution isn't objecting and there's a document that you need for your Defence, what do you propose to do if you aren't going to exhibit it at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I understood that your ruling was that we will follow the guide-lines. I failed. The Prosecution raised the issue. Your Honours ruled, and I withdrew the document. That is why -- I meant no disrespect to the Trial Chamber of course. I was -- it was just a comment to Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We understand, Mr. Zecevic, and we will also understand the basis for your objection if and when the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's exactly what I was doing, preserving my right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. This document is Prosecution exhibit from the 65 ter list. It will become exhibit for the Defence. Can the witness be shown the second -- [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page 2 of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, while we're struggling with the page, this is 65 ter number 690, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But I wanted the second page. The first one is just the cover page for the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djekanovic, this is an order by the Crisis Staff to impose a curfew in the Kotor Varos municipality dated the 12th of June, 1992. It has a number, and it's signed by you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You recognise this order, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D24, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown document 1D00-0751.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djekanovic, could you please look at this document. It's an excerpt from the minutes of the Crisis Staff meeting of the 20th of June, 1992. Is that correct? That's what it says in the heading.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please look at page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature, Mr. Djekanovic, in your capacity as president of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this document tendered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic. What -- before we put it into evidence, what exactly do you wish to draw the Court's attention to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we are having -- we will be having Ms. Hanson as the OTP expert on Crisis Staffs in very imminent future, I guess next week or the week after, something. Now, we have a number of documents which pertain to the Crisis Staff of Kotor Varos. As Mr. Djekanovic was the president of the Crisis Staff of Kotor Varos, he signed these minutes, and this is the only way which I see appropriate to tender this as exhibits because there will be no other way for us to tender these exhibits before Ms. Hanson appears -- appears in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I understand that, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And -- yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- you see, the reason I'm asking this is I want to be sure that in the end when the trial is over and the Chamber has withdrawn to deliberate, then we will come across this document and we will all wonder: Why on earth was this document put into evidence? It shows that there was an SDS Crisis Staff in Kotor Varos; that I think is not disputed. It shows that the witness was the president; that too is obvious and not disputed. So unless -- unless there's something in the contents of the document that you specifically want to draw the Court's attention to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There is definitely a lot of the specifics in these documents which I need for the cross-examination of the expert Ms. Hanson. But if Your Honours want me, I can file a bar table motion and explain the relevance of each and every of these documents. Because I thought it would be appropriate that I tender these documents as exhibits and then discuss them with Ms. Hanson because that is -- that was my intention. I don't need to -- I don't need to discuss this with the witness, as he can confirm only the authenticity. That is the only purpose. There is nothing that I need from these documents from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Except maybe a line or two on some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's on our 65 ter list, which takes -- makes the point that we thought it was relevant to an issue. It is actually relevant to an issue. I'm not inviting Mr. Zecevic to make a speech about why it is relevant, but it is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, again, I wasn't making a speech, I just --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, I'm just saying to avoid you making a speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just answering the Trial Chamber's question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not criticising you, Mr. Zecevic. I'm just saying that it didn't need a speech. I accept that it's relevant to an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Okay. I will -- the Chamber will accept this, but maybe we should bring it up in this 65 ter meeting later on. I mean, to find some sort of form of showing to the Chamber the relevance of documents as we admit them, I think that would be preferable. I don't mind you putting in this document at this time and then taking it up again with Ms. Hanson --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Sorry, let's stop here and just proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D25, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is -- I'm sorry, I just lost -- it's admitted. Thank you. Can the witness be shown document 1D00-0755.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, we're just up on the break now. Do you wish to do this now or when we return?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As it pleases the Court, Your Honours. It's time to rise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before we begin I would just like to apologise once again to the interpreters. I've been warned during the break about my speed, and I'm going to try to do my best to go slower, and I apologise once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: While we wait for the witness to come in, maybe we can just raise the venue for this afternoon's meeting, and I understand that the little conference room is booked. The big conference room upstairs is available only between 2.00 and 4.00, and therefore it was suggested that why don't we use a courtroom. And it turns out that Courtroom III is available this afternoon, so the deal is therefore that we'll meet informally, that is, not robed, in Courtroom III and use it as a conference room simply for this afternoon's meeting, and that will give us also the advantage of being able to use the computers. We had anticipated that we would start the meeting at 2.00, so we could either stop five minutes before and have a 20-minutes' break, or we could simply say that we'll stop at a quarter to 2.00 and then just not begin the meeting until 2.15. I don't know which -- it seems to me to be more gentle to have half an hour's lunch break. So maybe we should re-schedule and say that the meeting will start at 2.15 in Courtroom III. Is that acceptable to the parties?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the document that I asked for, 1D00-0755.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djekanovic, can you please look at the document. This is an excerpt of the minutes from the 33rd meeting of the Crisis Staff, and it was held on the 22nd of June, 1992, and your signature is at the bottom. Do you recall this document?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So it's your document?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Document that you signed?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, as with the last document, it would be useful to indicate the connection. It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, again, Your Honours, this is the very same situation and I have, like, ten other documents precisely the same and for the same purpose. Your Honours, one thing I believe should be said. There is no objection from the Prosecution side. That would suggest that the Prosecutor is fine with this document, and I'm just -- I'm just still getting this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please don't misunderstand me. The Chamber isn't saying that it shouldn't be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It's just that in the process of admitting it, it would be useful where it is obvious what the relevance is to indicate the purpose at this stage while you were -- while you're seeking -- while you're tendering it to indicate why it's being admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tried to explain. Maybe I should endeavour a bit more. The purpose of introducing these documents is to create the body of evidence which will be commented and shown to the expert -- to the OTP expert, Ms. Dorothea Hanson, and she's -- precisely for the purpose of explaining the Crisis Staff, she would be called to appear before the Trial Chamber and comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And that holds good for each of these ten documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Your Honour. I thought that you understood -- I meant as a whole body of documents I have I believe 15 documents, except one or two they're all of the same provenance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic. The lack of understanding is personal to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, why don't you then just throw the whole batch at us, just in one cut we can take it all rather than having to -- if what you're saying is that you will bring up each of these documents at a later stage with Mrs. Hanson and during your cross-examination of Mrs. Hanson and using these documents, then we will be led to understand why they're relevant. If that is the case, then let's just have them all in one batch now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, there are two things: Should I do it as a bar table motion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This is a matter of simple choice. You can do it through this witness if you feel comfortable with that and he is the author of them so it's perfectly legitimate to have them come in through him, or you can do it as a bar table motion -- my suggestion was just to save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, I understand. I'm perfectly willing to accommodate the Trial Chamber. I'm just wondering how to do it. I have the hard copies with me, so maybe I can give the hard copies of these documents to the witness, witness reviews them for, like, couple of minutes just to see if it's the minutes of the Crisis Staff, his signatures, and then I list, and then I read all these -- all their numbers, and they're admitted as exhibits with the appropriate exhibit number, if that is okay with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I have absolutely no objection to that course at all. I suggest also that we really ought to discuss in the 65 ter conference this business of explanations being given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So go ahead, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Zecevic could be kind enough just to read out the numbers so that we know which they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. The document -- the first document is 1D00-763 [sic] -- I'll speak in Serbian, I'm sorry. [Interpretation] Then 1D00-0775, 1D00-0777, 1D00-0779, 1D00-3447, 1D00-3118, 65 ter 00735, then 65 ter 00684 -- [In English] I suggest, Your Honours, while I'm reading this maybe the usher can give it to the usher so that he can review the documents if Ms. Korner has nothing against that. I suggested that I give the other documents to the witness for review while I read the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 12 documents in all, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit numbers are therefore 1D26, 1D27, 1D28, 1D29, 1D30, 1D31, 1D32, 1D33, 1D34, 1D35, 1D36, 1D37, and 1D38.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djekanovic, have you looked at these documents? Are they all documents of the Crisis Staff and then beginning with 1D00-0775, now 1D27 -- sorry, 1D28 is the first document related to the War Presidency, starting with June, and all the later documents are documents of the War Presidency. Have you looked through all of them?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have glanced through them. I haven't really reviewed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but they are minutes of the sessions of the Crisis Staff and minutes of the War Presidency and you've signed a great number of them?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are minutes of the Crisis Staff and War Presidency. I signed most of them, not all, but I don't question their authenticity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to bring the documents back to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djekanovic. Could you tell me, in addition to the fact that you were a deputy to the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, you were also a deputy to the Assembly of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In your examination-in-chief my learned friend asked you whether you had attended the session of the Assembly of Republika Srpska of the 12th of May in Banja Luka, and you confirmed; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, these Assembly sessions, you did not attend them only when it was impossible to go there because roads were blocked, that's May through July 1992, until the corridor was made in north Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know how many sessions I missed in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You touched upon in the direct examination the situation in Kotor Varos municipality in the period May through July 1992. Tell me, in the second half of June and in July, was there electricity available?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the time not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "most of the time," do you mean really most of the time or on most of the territory or both?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the time in a large part of the territory, and in some areas not at all. I know that because we had huge problems with water-supply, and we had to mount aggregates and pumps and supply water in this way to cities and towns. I know it also from many other things such as sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, telephone lines were also cut off; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The greatest part of that period, no telephone communications were available at all. Only later did we establish one telephone line through the post office in Banja Luka, but that was much later. In those first days we had no telephones at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You mean to say that there was one telephone line -- first of all, at the beginning there was no communication with the outside world, and then later one telephone line was established for the whole of the municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm talking about the whole of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So your only means of communication, apart from your physical ability or inability to leave the municipality and then only to Banja Luka, was this one telephone that was made to work?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in that period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly in your direct examination it was not safe to travel because there were ambushes along roads and other dangers?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June the road between Kotor Varos and Banja Luka was not safe at all. A number of people were wounded, even killed, especially the fork-offs towards Grabovica and other places where ambushes were set up daily.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: They were set up by the Muslim and the Croat armies; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite clear, armed forces who were not with us and there were other troops beside them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So the situation in the municipality in June and July 1992, if I understood correctly what you said now, first you had no power, no telephone communication, and the fact that there was no electricity makes it difficult to supply water. And you also had the problem of refugees coming from villages across the municipality to the town of Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a problem with refugees who escaped along the front lines towards town. We had the problem of fuel. We had had refugees in Kotor Varos from before, refugees from Croatia, and why did they come to Kotor Varos? Because in 1970s they bought land in Kotor Varos -- sorry, they had bought land in Croatia and moved there, but when things got rough there they returned to Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you speak of those refugees from Croatia, you mean Serbs who had lived in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Serbs who had fled from Croatia to Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: However, in addition to Serb refugees, there were also Croat and Muslim refugees; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June, certainly. As I said in my previous testimony, people were leaving their villages and looking for a safe place, looking for protection from us in the municipality. Some of them asked us to transport them - some people would call it escorting them out. Anyway, they wanted safe accommodation until transport was available, and there were cases when Muslim families or Croat families from more remote villages would come to town and find accommodation in the houses of their compatriots.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "protection," they were seeking protection from the war, from the conflicts that had engulfed their villages?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was a by-product of armed conflict. There were always people coming with completely different intentions, but most of them were people who fled before armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately how many refugees you had in Kotor Varos, the ratio of refugees to the population, the pre-war population?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In certain periods there were over 1.000 or 1500 refugees of Serb ethnicity, those from Croatia, from the Travnik municipality and some parts of our own municipality. And as for refugees who had just fled to save their lives of other ethnicities, those refugees did not stay with us long; they were just waiting for transport to other places and they were provisionally accommodated. We've discussed this at length here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you mention the sawing mill in direct examination, you were shown Exhibit P46, and you confirmed that the Crisis Staff had established that collection centre?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had come to an agreement that we had no better accommodation to offer. It used to be a restaurant, the cafeteria, the canteen of this sawing mill, and there were also some workshops empty of equipment available for accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now show the witness P66.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You remember this map where you marked the location of the public security station. I'm more interested now in that last photograph on the right showing the prison in Kotor Varos. That is the remand prison next to the court building, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was a prison used for a certain period before 1970 as a remand facility, and from then until 1992 it was simply not used. In 1992 it was again re-activated as a detention facility and has never been used as anything else but a prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But as a remand prison; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a remand prison. It's just behind the court building.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This prison in Maslovare on the territory of your municipality, it was a military prison, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, I don't remember any prisons in Maslovare. I know that some people were taken there. I don't know whether they spent the night, but they were not there for long. It was a military prison because there was no police and especially no court guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Maybe it's my mistake. Maybe it was not a prison. Maybe it was a collection centre, but at any rate it was under military control?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was under military control.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During your direct examination you will remember that my learned friend asked you about that fire at the Catholic church, it was the 9th of October, page 73 of the transcript, lines 16 through 23, you do remember, don't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the incident. I remember being asked about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djekanovic, do you know that the public security station filed a criminal complaint to the competent prosecutor's office after that prosecutor's office had been set up pertaining to that incident?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that I knew about it, but I can't recall it now. At any rate, I know about the fire. I know that we responded. I remember we did something but I can't recall what.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you show 1D00-0821. Could we zoom in a little. Could I have the Serbian version, please. No, this is -- that's a different document. I need 1D00-0821. The English document is correct but not the Serbian one. Used to be the right one, but then you pulled it down. That's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: First of all, let me ask you, when was the prosecutor's office established and when did it become operative in Kotor Varos municipality after May-June 1992, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact dates. I'm not even sure it ever stopped working. The judicial and prosecution authorities worked continuously, I think, and the reason I remember this is I remember discussions about who's going to be the prosecutor, who's going to the front line, et cetera, so I'm pretty sure that the judicial authorities and the prosecution continued to work throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you look at the criminal report on the left. It's a criminal complaint against an unidentified perpetrator or perpetrators pursuant to Article 172, paragraph 1, in Article 177 causing public danger at the detriment of the Roman Catholic church in Kotor Varos. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the witness the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just one question, this document was signed by Savo Tepic, chief of SUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was chief at the time, and I think I see his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Attached to this criminal report is an Official Note, saying that on the 2nd July 1992 at 12.30 a report was received that the Roman Catholic church had been set on fire, and the whole incident is explained, and the Official Note bears this date; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the church was set on fire on the 2nd July, is it your recollection?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can recollect the approximate time. I can't say whether it was the 2nd or the 5th, but I remember the day when it was set on fire. I know where I was then and how I reacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to doubt that this Official Note is correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No reason whatsoever especially because this person who signed on the document was an inspector of the police station, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe, Your Honours, that the witness has provided sufficient explanation, and if there is no objection from the Prosecution, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D39, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The last subject for today is the police. On the first day of your direct examination led by my learned friend Ms. Korner on page 56, date 8 October, line 10, you started saying that you had attended a meeting with the police with Ante Mandic. My colleague asked you about it, but what can you remember about this meeting? What was discussed with the police? Anto Mandic was the president of the municipality and you were the president of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in this capacity you went to that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That meeting was held in the pensioners' community hall next to the church, and representatives of all agencies in Kotor Varos was present. And we went there as, let's say, political leaders. But there was also a representative from the SDA party, and we were also trying to persuade each other and the police how law and order should be protected, that everyone should stay on the police force and do their jobs. We were simply trying to maintain law and order together. Let me just say again something that I've mentioned before. At the time when we were holding this meeting attended by all representatives of the police, there was a skirmish, an exchange of fire, before the pensioners' community hall. There was this man Sprzo and some other people going along the streets, firing into the air, running people down. It was a general chase all over town and shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead, but a little more slowly for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's just what I wanted to add. That's this meeting, although we had more than one meeting concerning the need to maintain law and order, the community spirit, et cetera. But we said one thing at meetings and quite another thing happened in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The person who shooted [sic] at the pensioners' hall, it was a member of HVO. Maybe we could clarify that with the witness because it is not in the transcript I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djekanovic, you heard my colleague. You mentioned the name of that gentleman, member of the HVO, who while you were having that meeting in the pensioners' hall led a group of HVO that shooted [as interpreted] from fire-arms. Could you just say his name slowly?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC [Resumed]
